summary:
PyroSync is a web app that fuses MODIS and VIIRS satellite fire data into one calibrated, continuous record. It ingests live NASA FIRMS data or CSV files from five satellites, then normalizes, merges and calibrates detections. Results appear on an interactive map, a burning calendar and a trend view, and can be exported as GeoJSON or CSV.
MODIS and VIIRS differ in resolution, and VIIRS reports 5–15× more hotspots, so raw counts can't be compared. PyroSync corrects pixel geometry, merges duplicate detections into single fire events, and models small-fire detection to keep trends seamless as MODIS retires.

Without harmonization, the 20+ year fire record breaks at the MODIS-to-VIIRS handover. One consistent record gives responders, scientists and land managers early warning, smarter monitoring and faster response.
details:
PyroSync is a NASA Space Apps Challenge project that merges two generations of NASA wildfire satellite data into one consistent record.

What it does / how it works

• NASA's older MODIS sensors (1 km resolution, being retired) and newer VIIRS sensors (375 m) detect fires differently. VIIRS sees 5-15x more hotspots, so mixing raw counts creates false spikes and double-counting.

• PyroSync fixes this in three steps:

1. Footprint geometry: it normalizes Fire Radiative Power (FRP) by true pixel area and overpass time. MODIS pixels stretch up to 4.5 km² at swath edges.

2. Deduplication: it clusters detections from Terra, Aqua, SNPP, NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 within a space-time window into single "Unified Fire Events."

3. Continuity bridge: it models small-fire detection probability so long-term trends stay continuous as MODIS retires.

• The dashboard has an interactive map (MODIS and VIIRS pixel boxes, fused-event circles), a continuity trend, a burning calendar, a 1:1 calibration plot and a top-events table. You can pull live NASA FIRMS data with your own MAP_KEY, upload a CSV, or export GeoJSON/CSV.

Benefits

• Fewer false spikes and duplicate counts.

• Small fires that MODIS misses are still resolved.

• Reduced cross-sensor bias, with R² and RMSE reported before and after.

• Adjustable parameters (fusion radius, overpass window, minimum confidence).

• Works with live global data or your own files.

Intended impact

• A continuous 2018-2026 fire record, so climate researchers, fire agencies and land managers can track multi-decade trends without a break when MODIS ends.

• More trustworthy burned-area and heat estimates for planning and response.

Tools and technology

• Visible from the site: it's a web app hosted on Vercel, using NASA FIRMS data (MODIS, VIIRS SNPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21).

• Not visible from the site: the exact frameworks, libraries and languages. It's most likely HTML/CSS/JavaScript with a mapping library, but please confirm this from your own repo.

• No special hardware is needed. It runs in the browser using satellite data.

Creativity

• It treats MODIS-to-VIIRS continuity as a calibration problem. It corrects pixel geometry and detection-probability differences instead of just merging datasets.

• The map shows each sensor's actual pixel footprint, with color-coded boxes and circles.

• You can play the timeline, filter by calendar day, and switch between MODIS-equivalent and VIIRS-equivalent reference frames.

Factors considered

• Resolution differences (1 km vs 375 m) and pixel distortion at swath edges.

• Different overpass times across five satellites.

• Detection confidence thresholds.

• The risk of double-counting heat.

• MODIS's retirement and long-term climate-record continuity.

• Usability: live queries (1-10 day lookback, any region), custom CSVs and exports.
